question.problem:
Find $\text{E}[{X}^{2}{Y}^{2}],$ given that random variables $X$ and $Y$ have the joint probability density function

$$
f(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}y+1,\, & 0\le x\le 2,\,-1\le y\le 0, \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}.\end{aligned}
$$
question.worked_solution:
Suppose $X$ and $Y$ are continuous random variables, and $f(x,y)$ is their joint probability density function. If $r:{R}^{2}\to R$ is a function of two variables, then the rule of the lazy statistician states that

$$
\text{E}[r(X,Y)]={∬}_{{R}^{2}}r(x,y)\,f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\text{d}y.
$$

In our case, we have

$$
r(x,y)={x}^{2}{y}^{2}.
$$

Notice that $f(x,y)$ is nonzero only in the rectangular region $D=\{(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 2,\,-1\le y\le 0\}.$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{2}{Y}^{2}] & ={∬}_{{R}^{2}}{x}^{2}{y}^{2}\,f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\text{d}y \\  & ={∬}_{D}{x}^{2}{y}^{2}\,f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{0}{\int }_{0}^{2}{x}^{2}{y}^{2}\cdot (y+1)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{0}({y}^{3}+{y}^{2}){\int }_{0}^{2}{x}^{2}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{0}({y}^{3}+{y}^{2}){[\frac{{x}^{3}}{3}]}_{0}^{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{0}\frac{8}{3}({y}^{3}+{y}^{2})\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{8}{3}[\frac{{y}^{4}}{4}+\frac{{y}^{3}}{3}]_{-1}^{0} \\  & =\frac{8}{3}(\frac{1}{3}-\frac{1}{4}) \\  & =\frac{2}{9}.\end{aligned}
$$
